title: Yenisey mean winter log curvature was negative in 30 certified winters from 1981 to 2011
abstract: We tested a passive parallel-store constraint in ArcticGRO v20261104 flow records at Ob, Lena and Yenisey. Three 28-day windows from 1 January gave mean log curvature of -0.02937 at Yenisey in 30 common certified winters from 1981 to 2011. The approximate simultaneous 95% interval across three rivers was -0.05643 to -0.00429 with three-year blocks. Five-year limits also stayed below zero. However, only nine Yenisey winters had declining means. Thus, this is a flow-shape result, not evidence of faster drainage. Lena declined in all 30 winters, but its primary interval narrowly included zero. Results depended on window dates. A uniform log-error allowance of 0.00734 can remove the negative Yenisey aggregate sign, without restoring a full passive-store model. Ice effects, regulation, inputs, source uncertainty and a selected short record limit physical inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, a figure and an independent arithmetic audit support reproduction. External records stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Mean log curvature across fixed winter windows. Passive parallel exponential stores require nonnegative curvature. Primary limits use three-year blocks and a Bonferroni adjustment across three rivers. The other windows show seasonal dependence.
